rows.acip: NYAN RANG DGRA BCOM PA CHOS CAN, PHYI ROL PA BZHIN DU KHAMS GSUM NA SPYOD PA'I PHRA RGYAS THAMS CAD MA SPANGS PAR THAL, DE THAMS CAD KYI RTZA BAR GYUR PA'I DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA DANG 'DZIN STANGS DNGOS 'GAL DU ZHUGS PA'I LAM MA RNYED PA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN MED PAR YONGS SU SHES PA DANG BRAL BA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: nyan rang dgra bcom pa chos can, phyi rol pa bzhin du khams gsum na spyod pa'i phra rgyas thams cad ma spangs par thal, de thams cad kyi rtsa bar gyur pa'i dngos po rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dzin pa'i rtog pa dang 'dzin stangs dngos 'gal du zhugs pa'i lam ma rnyed pa'i phyir, der thal, dngos po rang bzhin med par yongs su shes pa dang bral ba'i phyir
rows.english: Let us first consider enemy destroyers of the Listener or Self-Made Buddha type. Aren't you saying then that, like the non-Buddhists, they fail to eliminate all the widespread mental afflictions that operate in all three realms? Because isn't it true that they have failed to achieve the path which is directly incompatible, in the way it holds its object, with the root of all these afflictions; that is, the tendency to conceive of things as existing through some nature of their own? And this is true, for they lack that comprehensive knowledge where they realize that things have no nature of their own.

rows.acip: GZHAN YANG DE CHOS CAN, GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED RDZOGS PAR MA RTOGS PAR THAL, GANG ZAG RANG BZHIN MED PAR MNGON SUM DU MA RTOGS PA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, GDAGS GZHI PHUNG PO RANG NGOS NAS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I ZHEN YUL SUN 'BYIN MI NUS PA'I TSUL GYI PHYIN CI LOG GIS BCINGS PA YIN PA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, PHUNG PO RANG BZHIN MED PAR YONGS SU SHES PA DANG BRAL BA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: gzhan yang de chos can, gang zag gi bdag med rdzogs par ma rtogs par thal, gang zag rang bzhin med par mngon sum du ma rtogs pa'i phyir, der thal, gdags gzhi phung po rang ngos nas grub par 'dzin pa'i zhen yul sun 'byin mi nus pa'i tshul gyi phyin ci log gis bcings pa yin pa'i phyir, der thal, phung po rang bzhin med par yongs su shes pa dang bral ba'i phyir
rows.english: Consider these same enemy destroyers. It is true that they have not yet realized, entirely, the fact that the person has no self nature. This is because they have yet to perceive directly the fact that the person has no nature. This in itself is true as well, for they are still chained by total misperceptions, in such a way that they will never be able to root out the object that they think they see when they hold the parts to the person, the thing which gets the label of "me," as existing from its own side. And this too is true, for they lack that comprehensive knowledge where they realize that the parts to the person have no nature of their own.

rows.acip: THAL 'GYUR SNGA MA LA KHYAB PA YOD DE, GDAGS GZHI PHUNG PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA'I ZHEN YUL SUN PHYUNG MI NUS PA JI SRID 'JUG GI BAR DU, BTAGS CHOS GANG ZAG RANG NGOS NAS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA'I ZHEN YUL SUN PHYUNG MI NUS PAR 'JUG PA GANG ZHIG, DE JI SRID 'JUG GI BAR DU DE'I DBANG GIS LAS BSOG, LAS DE'I DBANG GIS 'KHOR BAR 'KHOR BA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: thal 'gyur snga ma la khyab pa yod de, gdags gzhi phung po rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dzin pa'i rtog pa'i zhen yul sun phyung mi nus pa ji srid 'jug gi bar du, btags chos gang zag rang ngos nas grub par 'dzin pa'i rtog pa'i zhen yul sun phyung mi nus par 'jug pa gang zhig, de ji srid 'jug gi bar du de'i dbang gis las bsog, las de'i dbang gis 'khor bar 'khor ba'i phyir
rows.english: The first of our logical statements above is always true. For suppose that a person is still unable to root out the object that he thinks he sees when he holds the parts to the person, the thing which gets the label of "me," as existing through some nature of its own. As long as he goes on this way, then he will continue to find himself unable to root out the object that he thinks he sees when he holds the thing which gets the label, the "me," as existing from its own side. And as long as he continues with this, then by the power of this misperception he will continue to collect karma. And as long as he collects karma, then he will continue to spin around in this wheel of suffering life. *********

rows.acip: RGYUD BLA MA RTZA 'GREL GYI DGONGS PA MTHAR THUG YIN TE, BDAG 'DZIN GNYIS KYI BAG CHAGS LA BRTEN NAS DE GNYIS SKYES, DE LA BRTEN NAS RANG NGOS NAS GRUB PA'I YID 'ONG BA DANG YID MI 'ONG DU SNANG BA'I TSUL MIN YID BYED KYI RNAM RTOG SKYE, DE LA BRTEN NAS YID 'ONG LA DMIGS NAS MI 'BRAL BAR 'DOD PA'I 'DOD CHAGS DANG , YID MI 'ONG LA DMIGS NAS 'BRAL 'DOD KYI ZHE SDANG SKYES, DE'I DBANG GIS LAS BSAGS LAS DE'I DBANG GIS 'KHOR BAR 'KHOR BA DANG DE LTAR 'KHOR BA DE YANG , DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I SNYING PO MNGON SUM DU MA RTOGS PA'I DBANG GIS YIN PAR GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR
rows.wylie: rgyud bla ma rtsa 'grel gyi dgongs pa mthar thug yin te, bdag 'dzin gnyis kyi bag chags la brten nas de gnyis skyes, de la brten nas rang ngos nas grub pa'i yid 'ong ba dang yid mi 'ong du snang ba'i tshul min yid byed kyi rnam rtog skye, de la brten nas yid 'ong la dmigs nas mi 'bral bar 'dod pa'i 'dod chags dang , yid mi 'ong la dmigs nas 'bral 'dod kyi zhe sdang skyes, de'i dbang gis las bsags las de'i dbang gis 'khor bar 'khor ba dang de ltar 'khor ba de yang , de bzhin gshegs pa'i snying po mngon sum du ma rtogs pa'i dbang gis yin par gsungs pa'i phyir
rows.english: This then is the ultimate idea within the root text and the commentary of the Higher Line, [written by Maitreya and Asanga]: Due to the mental seeds for the two kinds of tendencies to grasp to some self- nature, these two tendencies themselves spring up. Due to the fact that they have sprung up, an impression with a wrong way of looking at things springs up, and some things seem as though they are pleasant from their own side, and other things seem as though they are unpleasant from their own side. Due to the fact that this impression has sprung up, the emotion of liking springs up, where you focus on a pleasant object and don't want to lose it. And the emotion of disliking springs up, where you focus on an unpleasant object and want to avoid it. This then forces you to collect karma. And karma forces you to spin around in the wheel of suffering life. And this is why the Buddhas have said that this suffering life is something forced on us because we have not been able to see, directly, the essence of the Ones Gone Thus [that is, emptiness]. *********

rows.acip: CHU 'BAB KLUNG LA YI DVAGS RNAG BLO YANG , , ZHES SOGS KYI SKABS SU MTHA' DPYAD PA LA, CHU KLUNG RNAG KHRAG TU SNANG BA'I YI DVAGS KYI MIG SHES DANG , BSE RU'I NANG DU SKRA SHAD 'DZAG PAR SNANG BA'I RAB RIB CAN GYI MIG SHES DANG , SA GZHI KENG RUS KYIS KHYAB PAR SNANG BA'I KENG RUS GSAL SNANG CAN GYI TING NGE 'DZIN DANG BCAS PA RNAMS KYI YUL DE DANG , DER YOD MED RNAM PA KUN DU MTSUNGS SAM MI MTSUNGS ZHE NA,
rows.wylie: chu 'bab klung la yi dvags rnag blo yang , , zhes sogs kyi skabs su mtha' dpyad pa la, chu klung rnag khrag tu snang ba'i yi dvags kyi mig shes dang , bse ru'i nang du skra shad 'dzag par snang ba'i rab rib can gyi mig shes dang , sa gzhi keng rus kyis khyab par snang ba'i keng rus gsal snang can gyi ting nge 'dzin dang bcas pa rnams kyi yul de dang , der yod med rnam pa kun du mtshungs sam mi mtshungs zhe na
rows.english: Here we will analyze the statement [from Entering the Middle Way, by Master Chandrakirti (650 AD)] where it says, "...The mind of a craving spirit as well, which sees a stream of water as pus." One may begin with the following question: Let's consider the objects of the following states of mind: the visual consciousness of a craving spirit where a river of water looks like pus and blood; the visual consciousness of a person with a kind of cataract where a clean white porcelain basin looks like a hair has fallen into it; and that kind of meditation where you visualize skeletons--where you imagine that the entire surface of the earth is covered with the bones of corpses. Are all these objects completely equivalent, as far as being something that exists or doesn't exist?

rows.acip: KHA CIG NA RE, RGYU MTSAN DE NYID KYI PHYIR NA, CHOS THAMS CAD LA 'DI YIN 'DI MIN GANG DU YANG BZUNG DU MED DO, , ZHES ZER NA, SANGS RGYAS PA'I GRUB MTHA' DANG , PHYI ROL PA'I GRUB MTHA' LA BZANG NGAN DANG , BDAG CAG GI STON PA DANG , PHYI ROL PA'I STON PA LA MCHOG DMAN SOGS MED PAR THAL,
rows.wylie: kha cig na re, rgyu mtshan de nyid kyi phyir na, chos thams cad la 'di yin 'di min gang du yang bzung du med do, , zhes zer na, sangs rgyas pa'i grub mtha' dang , phyi rol pa'i grub mtha' la bzang ngan dang , bdag cag gi ston pa dang , phyi rol pa'i ston pa la mchog dman sogs med par thal
rows.english: Someone may make the following claim: Given the statements that have come above, the fact is that we should never again consider anything as being one way or the other. Well then, you must be suggesting that the system of the Buddha is all the same as the system of every non-Buddhist belief, that there is no difference in their correctness at all. And you must be saying too that we could never state that our Teacher was the highest teacher, and that the teachers of the non- Buddhists are lesser.

rows.acip: YANG KHA CIG, BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG LA, LHA MI YI DVAGS GSUM GYIS CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA, 'GRO BA RANG RANG GI NGO BOR THAD KA THAD KAR BDEN PAS, BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE, YI DVAGS KYI NGO BOR RNAG KHRAG TU BDEN, MI'I NGO BOR CHUR BDEN LHA'I NGO BOR BDUD RTZIR BDEN PA YIN NO, , ZER NA,
rows.wylie: yang kha cig, brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang la, lha mi yi dvags gsum gyis cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe na, 'gro ba rang rang gi ngo bor thad ka thad kar bden pas, brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de, yi dvags kyi ngo bor rnag khrag tu bden, mi'i ngo bor chur bden lha'i ngo bor bdud rtsir bden pa yin no, , zer na
rows.english: Someone else might make the following claim: Suppose a pleasure being, a human, and a craving spirit sit down together and look at a glass filled with water: the thing that we define as "wet and flowing." Since to the perceptions of each different type of being it is real, the glass full of wet and flowing water is in reality pus and blood to the eyes of the craving spirit, and in reality water to the eyes of the human, and in reality ambrosia to the eyes of the pleasure being.

rows.acip: DE'I TSE NA 'GRO BA GSUM PO DE'I MIG SHES THAMS CAD TSAD MA YIN NAM, 'GA' ZHIG TSAD MA YIN PA DAG LAS GANG YIN, DANG PO LTAR NA BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE RNAG KHRAG LA SOGS PA'I DNGOS PO GSUM GA YIN PA DANG , 'GAL BA LA MA 'KHRUL BA'I TSAD MA YOD PA DANG , PHOR PA GANG PO DE CHU YIN PA DANG CHU MA YIN PA GNYIS KAR TSAD MAS RTOGS PAR THAL, DE'I TSE NA 'GRO BA GSUM PO DE'I MIG SHES THAMS CAD TSAD MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: de'i tshe na 'gro ba gsum po de'i mig shes thams cad tshad ma yin nam, 'ga' zhig tshad ma yin pa dag las gang yin, dang po ltar na brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de rnag khrag la sogs pa'i dngos po gsum ga yin pa dang , 'gal ba la ma 'khrul ba'i tshad ma yod pa dang , phor pa gang po de chu yin pa dang chu ma yin pa gnyis kar tshad mas rtogs par thal, de'i tshe na 'gro ba gsum po de'i mig shes thams cad tshad ma yin pa'i phyir
rows.english: We ask you then a question: in the situation you've just described, is it that the visual consciousness of all three beings are a valid perception, or is it that only one or two of them are a valid perception? Suppose you say all three are valid. Well then, the glass of wet and flowing water must be full of something that is all three different things: pus and blood, and each of the others. And then too it must be possible for there to be multiple and yet still valid perceptions which see one thing in two completely incompatible ways. And finally there must be such a thing as a valid perception which correctly perceives that the glass is filled with something which is simultaneously water and yet not water. Why so? Because, according to your view, the three differing cases of visual consciousness possessed by the three different beings would all have to be valid perception.

rows.acip: 'DOD NA MI 'THAD PAR THAL, RNAG KHRAG LA SOGS PA'I DNGOS PO GSUM PO 'GAL BA'I PHYIR DANG , CHU YIN MIN GNYIS PO DE PHAN TSUN SPANGS 'GAL GYI DNGOS 'GAL YIN PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: 'dod na mi 'thad par thal, rnag khrag la sogs pa'i dngos po gsum po 'gal ba'i phyir dang , chu yin min gnyis po de phan tshun spangs 'gal gyi dngos 'gal yin pa'i phyir
rows.english: And if you try to agree to these absurdities, you are wrong, for the quality of being pus and blood is incompatible with the quality of being either one of the other two substances mentioned. Moreover, the quality of being water and the quality of not being water are directly incompatible in such a way that, if something exists and lacks one of these qualities, it must then possess the other.

rows.acip: 'O NA MI'I MIG SHES TSAD MA MA YIN PAR THAL, MI LAS 'BRING PO'I DBANG GIS CHUR MTHONG BA TZAM YIN PA'I PHYIR, GZHAN YANG , MI MA YIN PA'I 'GRO BA'I RGYUD LA LUS SHES TSAD MA DANG , NYAN SHES TSAD MA YANG MED PAR THAL, DE'I RGYUD LA MIG SHES TSAD MA MED PA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, KHYOD KYI RTZA BA'I DAM BCA' 'THAD PA'I PHYIR, 'DOD NA,
rows.wylie: 'o na mi'i mig shes tshad ma ma yin par thal, mi las 'bring po'i dbang gis chur mthong ba tsam yin pa'i phyir, gzhan yang , mi ma yin pa'i 'gro ba'i rgyud la lus shes tshad ma dang , nyan shes tshad ma yang med par thal, de'i rgyud la mig shes tshad ma med pa'i phyir, der thal, khyod kyi rtsa ba'i dam bca' 'thad pa'i phyir, 'dod na
rows.english: Well then, according to you, the visual consciousness of the human wouldn't be valid perception either. Because isn't it true that the human sees the water only because his karma (which in this case is halfway between the good and the bad just mentioned) forces him to? Moreover, aren't you implying then that there is no such thing as a valid tactile consciousness, or a valid auditory consciousness, in the mental stream of any being who is not a human? Because aren't you saying that there's no such thing as a valid visual consciousness in the mental stream of any such being? Certainly you are, for you believe your original position to be correct. And suppose now that you do agree that such beings can have no such valid consciousnesses.

rows.wylie: `gnyis pa rang lugs bzhag pa la, brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang la, las can gyi lha mi yi dvags gsum gyis cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe, chu phor pa gang po de dngos po gsum gyi gzhi mthun pa ma yin pa dang , de'i tshe tshad mtshungs gsum nges par mi dgos shing , brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de cha shas gsum ldan du skye ba dang
rows.english: Here secondly is the section where we establish our own position. Now suppose three different types of beings--a pleasure being, a human, and a craving spirit, each with their own karma--sit down together and look upon a glass filled with water, the thing we define as "wet and flowing." The glass of water is not at this point one thing which is simultaneously three different objects. Neither is it necessary in this situation for there to be three identical valid perceptions. And when the glass full of wet and flowing water occurs, it occurs with three different, distinct parts to it.

rows.acip: DE YANG DANG POR GRUB TZAM NAS CHA SHAS GSUM LDAN DU GRUB CING , MTHAR MA ZHIG GI BAR DU CHA SHAS GSUM LDAN DU GNAS PA MA YIN TE, BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE'I CHA SHAS GCIG GIS NYER LEN DANG , YI DVAGS KYI LAS KYIS LHAN CIG BYED RKYEN BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS DE'I CHA SHAS GCIG GI RIGS 'DRA PHYI MA RNAG KHRAG TU SKYE BA DANG ,
rows.wylie: de yang dang por grub tsam nas cha shas gsum ldan du grub cing , mthar ma zhig gi bar du cha shas gsum ldan du gnas pa ma yin te, brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de'i cha shas gcig gis nyer len dang , yi dvags kyi las kyis lhan cig byed rkyen byas pa la brten nas de'i cha shas gcig gi rigs 'dra phyi ma rnag khrag tu skye ba dang
rows.english: It is not though the case that, from the time it first started, the glass of water came with the three different parts, or that they stay with the glass of water until it eventually ends. What happens is that one of the parts of the glass filled with wet and flowing water provides a material cause, and the karma of the craving spirit provides a contributing factor; and then based on both of these the later continuation of one part of the glass of water starts being blood and pus.

rows.english: There is, moreover, an example we can use for how, when the three different types of beings with their three karmas look all together at a glass full of something wet and flowing, there start to be three different objects, each confirmed by a valid perception. rows.english: Here is the third part of our presentation, where we refute the rebuttal of representatives of other views. You will recall that our own position is describing a situation where beings of three different types, each with their own karma, are sitting together and looking at a glass filled with something that is wet and flowing. The glass filled with something wet and flowing exists, at this point, as something with three distinct parts. rows.english: One comes and makes the following claim: Your position, as just explained, is mistaken, for it goes against a statement of the glorious Dharmakirti. This is quite surely the case, for in his major work [entitled The Commentary on Valid Perception] he says, Suppose you say that they don't see it, And circumstances cause another form. What he's talking about here is a belief of the [non- Buddhist] Numerist School. They give the case of a single person whose physical form is looked upon at the same time by his enemy, and also by his friend. In reality, the person's physical form is both attractive and ugly at the same time. Something happens where yet another physical form, one from karma, grows up between the person's true physical form and the enemy and friend looking at it. Because of this neither the enemy nor the friend sees both the attractiveness and the ugliness together. Master Dharmakirti uses logic to refute this concept, and this same logic can be used against the position you have taken, to prove that you are wrong.

rows.english: This is a fact, for the actual meaning of Master Dharmakirti's statement is as follows. The Numerist School is describing a situation where you are looking at a physical form either from far away, or from up close. They say that, depending on the distance between you and the object, another physical form which is the result of karma, and which stands between your visual consciousness and the original form, is either clear or not. This then determines whether the original form appears to you distinctly or not. It is not the case though, they say, that what determines whether the original form appears clearly or not is whether or not you have a clear impression of this form. In reply then Master Dharmakirti is asking the Numerists: Let's consider these two cases of some intermediate physical form that comes from karma. Do they, or do they not, function to obscure the two original forms, the one at a distance, and the other close by? If they were to obscure them, then your visual consciousness could never see the two original forms, since they would have been obscured by the others.

rows.wylie: gnyis pa der thal, phyogs snga mas brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la, 'gro ba gsum gyis cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe na, brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang po de, dngos po gsum gyi gzhi mthun du yang khas ma blangs, skyes bu gcig gi gzugs mdzes mi mdzes gnyis ka yin par yang khas ma blangs, yi dvags kyis mig shes dang chu klung gi bar du rnag khrag gi las gzugs skye bar khas ma blangs, yi dvags kyi mig gis rnag khrag gi las gzugs dang chu klung gnyis ka mthong bar yang khas ma blangs, las kyi dbang gis yi dvags kyi chu klung ma mthong bar khas blangs pa'i phyir
rows.english: Our second point [that you have failed to comprehend the position we expressed above] is also quite true. Our original position was describing a situation where three different kinds of beings were sitting together and looking at a glass full of something wet and flowing. It is not our position that the glass full of something wet and flowing is one thing that is three different things. And it is not our position that there is such a thing as the physical appearance of a person which is at once both attractive and ugly. It is furthermore not our position that the blood and pus represent some kind of physical form which results from karma and grows up between the visual consciousness of the craving spirit and the stream of water. And it is not our position that the craving spirit's eyes see both this blood and pus as some kind of physical form resulting from karma, and the river of water at the same time. It is our position that, by force of his karma, the craving spirit is not able to see the stream of water.

rows.acip: GZHAN YANG , DPAL CHOS KYI GRAGS PA'I LUNG DANG KHYOD 'GAL BA YIN TE, KHYOD KYI NAD LNGA DANG , 'BYUNG BA LNGA DANG , GDON LNGA DANG BCAS PA RNAMS, NYON MONGS PA DUG LNGA'I DNGOS 'BRAS SU KHAS BLANGS, MU STEGS BYED KYI BAD KAN DANG 'DOD CHAGS RGYU 'BRAS, MKHRIS PA DANG ZHE SDANG RGYU 'BRAS SOGS SU KHAS BLANGS PA LA, BAD KAN DANG 'DOD CHAGS RJES SU 'GRO LDOG 'KHRUL, MKHRIS PA DANG ZHE SDANG RJES SU 'GRO LDOG 'KHRUL PAS DE 'GOG BYED KYI, 'KHRUL PHYIR RLUNG SOGS CHOS MA YIN, , ZHES PA'I GZHUNG 'DON PA SGYUR BA'I SGO NAS KHYOD LA GNOD PA'I PHYIR DANG , 'DUS MA BYAS KYI NAM MKHA' PHRAG DOG GI DNGOS 'BRAS SU 'DOD PA MI RIGS PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: gzhan yang , dpal chos kyi grags pa'i lung dang khyod 'gal ba yin te, khyod kyi nad lnga dang , 'byung ba lnga dang , gdon lnga dang bcas pa rnams, nyon mongs pa dug lnga'i dngos 'bras su khas blangs, mu stegs byed kyi bad kan dang 'dod chags rgyu 'bras, mkhris pa dang zhe sdang rgyu 'bras sogs su khas blangs pa la, bad kan dang 'dod chags rjes su 'gro ldog 'khrul, mkhris pa dang zhe sdang rjes su 'gro ldog 'khrul pas de 'gog byed kyi, 'khrul phyir rlung sogs chos ma yin, , zhes pa'i gzhung 'don pa sgyur ba'i sgo nas khyod la gnod pa'i phyir dang , 'dus ma byas kyi nam mkha' phrag dog gi dngos 'bras su 'dod pa mi rigs pa'i phyir
rows.english: And anyway, maybe it's you who have contradicted a statement of the glorious Dharmakirti. You have taken the position that the five sicknesses, and the five elements, and the five demons are all the direct result of the five poisons--the five bad thoughts. But when the non-Buddhists take the position that phlegm and desire have a cause-and-effect relationship, and that bile and anger have the same kind of relationship, and so on, then Master Dharmakirti refutes them by showing that desire doesn't always come and go according to the phlegm, and anger doesn't always come and go according to the bile. To do so he makes the statement that says, "It's not a fact that wind and the rest are such, for the relationship doesn't always hold." We could twist around this statement too and say that it disproved your position; and add as well how wrong it is to assert that uncreated space could ever be the direct result of jealousy. [The point seems to be that, although your position about the bad thoughts, and our original position on the nature of the three beings' perceptions, are both correct, you could always twist around some quotation by a master, take it out of context or misinterpret it, and try to show they were wrong.]

rows.english: There is, moreover, an example we can use for how, when the three different types of beings with their three karmas look all together at a glass full of something wet and flowing, there start to be three different objects, each confirmed by a valid perception. Suppose there is a ball of red-hot steel; one piece of this ball provides the material cause, and the "mantra of steel" provides a contributing factor. Due to these two, a person who has used the mantra of steel on his hand can touch the ball, but he doesn't undergo any sensation of heat; instead, he feels some other sensation. A person who has not used the mantra on his hand touches the ball and does feel a sensation of heat, and no other kind of sensation.

rows.english: That highest of Victors, the Great Fifth of the Dalai Lamas, has said as well, What happened before? Someone has been in my mind for time with no beginning. When was that? There's never been a moment when they were gone. Who are they? I live, and live again, the mental afflictions. And in the end? They will leave me to rot in the ocean of suffering life, without an end in sight. And the karma? It comes like the wind, with all the things I never wanted. How far? It whips around me everywhere, and stirs great waves, the three forms of suffering. How long? I could wander around this sea forever; the torch would spin, and the circle of light would blaze. What should I see? Think on this, and see that the afflictions of the mind are the one true enemy. What must be done? The enemy of living for this life must die. Who shall do it? rows.acip: DANG POR GANG DU GNAS PA DE YANG 'GRO BA GSUM PO DE'I RANG RANG GI THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I LAS LA BRTEN NAS GRUB PA'I SNOD KYI 'JIG RTEN GANG NAS BLANGS PA DE NYID DU GRUB PA YIN TE, MI'I THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I LAS LA BRTEN NAS GRUB PAS MI'I 'JIG RTEN GYI CHU DVANGS SHING BSIL BA NAS BLANGS NA DE NYID DU GNAS PA SOGS YIN PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: dang por gang du gnas pa de yang 'gro ba gsum po de'i rang rang gi thun mong ma yin pa'i las la brten nas grub pa'i snod kyi 'jig rten gang nas blangs pa de nyid du grub pa yin te, mi'i thun mong ma yin pa'i las la brten nas grub pas mi'i 'jig rten gyi chu dvangs shing bsil ba nas blangs na de nyid du gnas pa sogs yin pa'i phyir
rows.english: How the glass of liquid exists originally all depends on the particular outer world from where it has been taken, for each of the three different beings has a different outer world, depending on the specific karma he himself has collected. If the glass of liquid were sweet, cool water taken from the world of humans--a world created by the specific karma of the human in the group--then that would be its original condition, and so on.

rows.acip: GSAL CHA DANG DVANGS CHA NI YUL LA MI BYED PAR, YUL CAN SHES PA LA GSAL CHA'AM DVANGS CHA YOD MED LA BYA DGOS, GSAL CHA MI 'BYUNG BA'I TSE SGRIB BYED KYIS SGRIB PA LTAR YOD,
rows.wylie: gsal cha dang dvangs cha ni yul la mi byed par, yul can shes pa la gsal cha'am dvangs cha yod med la bya dgos, gsal cha mi 'byung ba'i tshe sgrib byed kyis sgrib pa ltar yod
rows.english: It's important to say here that—when we talk about clarity, or clearness—we're not talking about a quality of the object. Rather, it's a distinction that you have to make about the subject state of mind in meditation: does the mind itself feel clear—is there mental clarity, or not? When we can't get clarity to come, it feels almost like we've moved under a dark shadow.

rows.english: Human beings perceive it as water which is sweet and clear and cool, and relate to it by saying, “I'll take a bath in it,” or “I'll take a drink from it.” Those worldly gods who are deep in meditation upon the absorption known as “Limitless Space” see the same thing as empty space, for their conception of it as form has dissolved completely.

rows.english: It happened one day In a moment of mental clarity-- I was thinking a bit On the essence of all the teachings I'd heard, And the thought Made my think of all the kindness That my Lama Had ever paid to me. And then I blurted out this Song of the Diamond, Which is meant To repay in some small way My Lord, My Lama, for all his kindness, Taking everything That I've gleaned from the years Of scripture, And whispered advice, and logic, And expressing it all In that extraordinary method Where you take the goal And use it as the path to the goal.

rows.english: These rays of light invite to you all the enlightened Victors of the entire universe, in limitless forms of the secret world of the shining Diamond Lord of Terror, and all the Holy Beings who reside in this world. rows.english: The way in which this body remains within the heap of the body which is a ripening of karma is like (10) the way that lightning flashes deep within a cloud. rows.acip: NYAL LUGS PHYI MA LTAR NA, NAM MKHA' STONG PA LAS SPRIN RDOL BA'AM, CHU DVANGS PA LAS NYE'U CHUNG 'PHAR BA BZHIN DU BDE CHEN 'OD GSAL STONG PA NYID KYI NGANG LAS RANG NYID RNAL 'BYOR MA'I SKUR LAM GYIS LDANG STE, GNAS SOGS KYI BKOD PA'I KHYAD PAR PHUN SUM TSOGS PAR MOS,
rows.wylie: nyal lugs phyi ma ltar na, nam mkha' stong pa las sprin rdol ba'am, chu dvangs pa las nye'u chung 'phar ba bzhin du bde chen 'od gsal stong pa nyid kyi ngang las rang nyid rnal 'byor ma'i skur lam gyis ldang ste, gnas sogs kyi bkod pa'i khyad par phun sum tshogs par mos
rows.english: If you have been sleeping the second way, imagine that you waken all in a flash, as the Angel Herself, from a state of emptiness, from great bliss and the clear light.  Picture it like the way a cloud pops up all of a sudden in a clear blue sky, or the way a tiny fish suddenly leaps out of a pool of crystal water.  Try hard to imagine then that the place and other things around you are all perfectly excellent.

rows.acip: BSGRUBS PA'I NANG MCHOD LAS LAG GA YON PA'I MTHEB SRIN GYIS BLANGS TE 'BRU GSUM BRJOD PA DANG SBRAGS LAG GA YAS PA'I MTHIL DU AOm RANG GI MDUN TSUR NGOS DANG, A'A: GA YAS, H'Um GA YON DU GNAS PAR BSAMS TE RTZE MO RANG LA BSTAN PA'I CHOS 'BYUNG GA YON SKOR DU BRIS PA'I DBUS NAS BDE STONG GNYIS SU MED PA'I YE SHES BDUD RTZI'I RNAM PAR SHAR BA'I SNYING PO BLANG BAR MOS NAS RANG LHAR GSAL BA'I LCER MYANG BA BAm YIG LA THIM PAS SNYIGS MA BSREGS, DVANGS MAS TSIMS NAS LUS THAMS CAD BDE BA CHEN PO'I YE SHES KYI BDUD RTZIS GANG ZHING, SDIG SGRIB NYES LTUNG THAMS CAD DAG PAR MOS SHING,
rows.wylie: bsgrubs pa'i nang mchod las lag ga yon pa'i mtheb srin gyis blangs te 'bru gsum brjod pa dang sbrags lag ga yas pa'i mthil du aoM rang gi mdun tshur ngos dang, a'a: ga yas, hUM ga yon du gnas par bsams te rtse mo rang la bstan pa'i chos 'byung ga yon skor du bris pa'i dbus nas bde stong gnyis su med pa'i ye shes bdud rtsi'i rnam par shar ba'i snying po blang bar mos nas rang lhar gsal ba'i lcer myang ba baM yig la thim pas snyigs ma bsregs, dvangs mas tshims nas lus thams cad bde ba chen po'i ye shes kyi bdud rtsis gang zhing, sdig sgrib nyes ltung thams cad dag par mos shing
rows.english: Hold this now in your right hand, and take out some of the liquid with the thumb and ring finger of your left hand.  As you say the three holy letters, draw a dharma star on the palm of your right hand, going around to the left as you make the lines.  The top corner of the star should be facing you, and imagine that the letter om is on the corner towards you; the ah is to the right; and the hung is to the left. Now pick up the liquid from the center of the star, with a strong feeling that you are taking up the very essence of wisdom which is made of bliss and emptiness inseparably combined, appearing in the form of nectar.  See yourself as the Angel, and touch the nectar to Your tongue. The nectar comes down and melts into the vam letter.  It burns away all the dregs inside, and fills you with refined essence.  Try to feel strongly that you are satiated with nectar of the wisdom of great bliss, and that all your bad deeds and obscurations, all the wrongful acts and downfalls you have committed against your vows and pledges, are completely cleaned away.

rows.acip: BDUD RTZI'I DVANGS MA RNAMS SANGS RGYAS THAMS CAD DANG RNAL 'BYOR MA'I THUGS RANG SEMS DANG GNYIS SU MED PA'I SNYING GA'I BAm YIG LA THIM PAS BAm YIG GZI BYIN LHAG PAR 'BAR ZHING BDE STONG GI YE SHES KHYAD PAR CAN SKYES PAR MOS PA THUGS KYI DGA' BA STE SKU GSUNG THUGS KYI DGA' BA GSUM DANG,

rows.english: The refined essences of the nectar melt into the letter vam at your heart, and this letter is the indivisible combination of your own thoughts and the holy mind of all the Buddhas and Angels.  Thinking strongly that this is happening--that it makes the letter blaze with even greater splendor and gives you extraordinary wisdom of bliss and emptiness--is the ecstasy of the holy mind.

rows.english: This nectar of wisdom fills every single corner of your body.  It cleans away each and every one of your negative deeds and obstacles, leaving you perfectly pure. Imagine then that the vam letter at your heart is in actuality every single Enlightened Being of the universe; the very essence of the nectar sinks into this letter, triggering within Them even more extraordinary realizations of the wisdom of undivided bliss and void.  See then that They are very, very pleased with you.

rows.acip: ZHAL GYI MCHU SGROS BIMPA LTAR DMAR PA, BIMPA NI RGYA GAR SKAD DE, BSGYUR NA GZUGS BRNYAN CAN, ZHES PAR 'GYUR, 'DI RGYA GAR NAS 'BYUNG ZHING, PHAL SKAD LA KANDHU RA ZER BA'I SHING THOG DMAR PO SHIN TU MDOG LEGS GSAL DVANGS PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS BRNYAN KYANG 'CHAR BZOD PA LTA BU ZHIG YIN GSUNGS,
rows.wylie: zhal gyi mchu sgros bimpa ltar dmar pa, bimpa ni rgya gar skad de, bsgyur na gzugs brnyan can, zhes par 'gyur, 'di rgya gar nas 'byung zhing, phal skad la kandhu ra zer ba'i shing thog dmar po shin tu mdog legs gsal dvangs phyi rol gyi gzugs brnyan kyang 'char bzod pa lta bu zhig yin gsungs
rows.english: The Angel's lips are red as the bimba.  The word bimba is Sanskrit, and translates into Tibetan as "the one with the reflection."  It is said that this refers to a fruit that comes from India, one that is commonly referred to as the kandhura.  The kandhura has a fine, vivid crimson color, and its surface is so bright that you can see your reflection in it.

rows.english: With the blessing of its presence, then inside the central channel at the navel, where the taste and solitary channels are entwined around it, is an eh letter29 in the shape of a triangle. rows.acip: DES NA DANG PO NAS RMI LAM GSAL BA DANG DE MIN KYANG GNAS DBEN PA LA SOGS PA RIG PA DVANGS PA'I RGYU'I KHYAD PAR TSOGS PA'I SKABS DANG, MTSAN MO GCIG GI'ANG THO RANGS LTA BU RIG PA GSAL DUS SU, RMI LAM ZIN PAR SLA'O,,
rows.wylie: des na dang po nas rmi lam gsal ba dang de min kyang gnas dben pa la sogs pa rig pa dvangs pa'i rgyu'i khyad par tshogs pa'i skabs dang, mtshan mo gcig gi'ang tho rangs lta bu rig pa gsal dus su, rmi lam zin par sla'o
rows.english: Given all this, it is easier to maintain recognition in your dreams under the following conditions. First, when your dreams are clearer in the first place. Secondly when, even if they are not normally clear, you have created a situation with all the special conditions that lend a lucid state of mind: staying in an isolated area, and the like. And finally, even with regard to a single night, those periods--such as daybreak--when your mental state is more clear.

rows.english: On the eight petals formed by the channels outside this piece are the eight letters ah, ka, cha, ta [retroflex], ta [normal], pa, ya, and sha.  On the 56 petals of the channels outside them are the 34 consonants of the Sanskrit alphabet, the 16 vowels, and the six short vowels of a, i, u, e, o, and ah.  These letters are pointing upright, and their actual nature is the refined essence of the substances.  Our Lama noted that the ah in Shalu's treatise with a small circle over it was again a printing error.

rows.acip: SNANG BA DE BSDUS PA'I RJES SU KOR LE RER THIG LE DKAR PO 'AM, ZLA BA SOGS 'CHAR BA'I DKAR LAM MIN PA'I YID NGOR GANG SNANG THAMS CAD NAM MKHA' GA-YA' DAG 'DRA BA ZHIG LA, ZLA 'OD SHIN TU DVANGS SHING GSAL BA SHAR BA 'DRA BA ZHIG GIS THAMS CAD DU KHYAB PA 'ONG STE, STONG PA DANG, SNANG BA ZHES ZER RO,,
rows.wylie: snang ba de bsdus pa'i rjes su kor le rer thig le dkar po 'am, zla ba sogs 'char ba'i dkar lam min pa'i yid ngor gang snang thams cad nam mkha' ga-ya' dag 'dra ba zhig la, zla 'od shin tu dvangs shing gsal ba shar ba 'dra ba zhig gis thams cad du khyab pa 'ong ste, stong pa dang, snang ba zhes zer ro

rows.acip: DES NA 'OD GSAL RLUNG STOBS KYIS ZIN PA MIN PAS, GNYID TING NGE 'DZIN DU SKYED NUS PA LA NI GNYID KYI 'OD GSAL GYI SNGON DU 'CHAR DGOS PA'I STONG PA GSUM SNGAR BSHAD PA DE MI 'CHAR BAS, DE GSUM SNGON DU MI 'CHAR BA'I GNYID KYI TING NGE 'DZIN GSAL DVANGS BYUNG YANG, GNYID KYI 'OD GSAL GYI DON MED DO,,
rows.wylie: des na 'od gsal rlung stobs kyis zin pa min pas, gnyid ting nge 'dzin du skyed nus pa la ni gnyid kyi 'od gsal gyi sngon du 'char dgos pa'i stong pa gsum sngar bshad pa de mi 'char bas, de gsum sngon du mi 'char ba'i gnyid kyi ting nge 'dzin gsal dvangs byung yang, gnyid kyi 'od gsal gyi don med do
rows.english: What this all means is that, because he or she has not attained recognition of the clear light by force of their work with their winds, then this individual who is able to maintain meditative concentration in their sleep has not managed to get the three types of emptiness to appear, as we described earlier, first--and the fact is that they must appear prior to the clear light of sleep.  And although it may be true that you can achieve a meditative concentration within your sleep which is extremely lucid even without these three having made their appearance, this is not what the "clear light of sleep" refers to.

rows.acip: DE'I PHYIR GNYID KYI 'OD GSAL LA NYAMS DANG RTOGS PA'I 'OD GSAL GNYIS DANG, SRAB MO DANG 'THUG PO'I 'OD GSAL GNYIS DANG, RMI LAM GYI DUS SU RTOG MED KYI TING NGE 'DZIN GSAL DVANGS BYUNG BA YANG, GNYID KYI 'OD GSAL DU 'JOG PA'I RNAM GZHAG MANG PO SNANG YANG SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR MA PHYED PAR GNYID TING NGE 'DZIN DU SKYED NUS PA TZAM GYI STENG NAS BSHAD PA MANG DU BYAS PAR SNANG BAS, YID BRTAN THUB PA MI SNANG NGO,,
rows.wylie: de'i phyir gnyid kyi 'od gsal la nyams dang rtogs pa'i 'od gsal gnyis dang, srab mo dang 'thug po'i 'od gsal gnyis dang, rmi lam gyi dus su rtog med kyi ting nge 'dzin gsal dvangs byung ba yang, gnyid kyi 'od gsal du 'jog pa'i rnam gzhag mang po snang yang sngar bshad pa ltar ma phyed par gnyid ting nge 'dzin du skyed nus pa tsam gyi steng nas bshad pa mang du byas par snang bas, yid brtan thub pa mi snang ngo
rows.english: And so it is that the clear light of sleep can be discussed in terms of the two of a feeling of clear light and an actual experience of clear light; and in terms of the two of a less deep state of clear light and a deeper state of it; and in terms of a clear and lucid state of non-conceptual concentration that comes in your dreams.  And despite the fact that many presentations on the clear light of sleep have been written, a great number of them give their explanation based on nothing more than teaching the ability to turn sleep into a state of meditative concentration, without making any of the distinctions we've just mentioned.  As such it does not appear that we should accept these words as authoritative.

rows.acip: YANG SNGAR BZHIN LAN BDUN TZAM BYAS PAS, STOD KYI KHAMS DVANGS MA THAMS CAD ZHU BA RO RKYANG BRGYUD DBU MAR ZHUGS PAS DBU MA PHAL CHER KHENGS, SMAD KYI KHAMS DVANGS MA RNAMS KYANG RO RKYANG DU ZHUGS SHING RO RKYANG GI MAR SNE DBU MAR BCUG PA NAS DRANGS PAS,
rows.wylie: yang sngar bzhin lan bdun tsam byas pas, stod kyi khams dvangs ma thams cad zhu ba ro rkyang brgyud dbu mar zhugs pas dbu ma phal cher khengs, smad kyi khams dvangs ma rnams kyang ro rkyang du zhugs shing ro rkyang gi mar sne dbu mar bcug pa nas drangs pas
rows.english: Stoke the fire seven more times, as before.  All of the purified essence residing in the upper parts of the body now melts into the channel of taste and the solitary channel.  From there it enters into the central channel, almost filling it. The purified essence in the lower parts of the body also enters into the taste and solitary channels.  From their lower openings, which are inserted into the central channel, it is drawn up into the central channel.

rows.english: The next step is to take a retention, as before, and watch as the purified essence of the substances within the channels of the upper part of the body come and fill the channel of taste, and the solitary channel.  They then flow into the central channel and fill most of it.

rows.acip: SMAD KYI KHAMS DVANGS MA RNAMS KYANG RO RKYANG GNYIS SU ZHUGS NAS RO RKYANG GNYIS KYI MAR SNE DBU MA'I NANG DU BCUG NAS KHAMS THAMS CAD DBU MAR ZHUGS PAS DBU MA SMIN MTSAMS NAS BHA GA'I BA'I BAR KHAMS DVANGS MA DNGUL CHU LTA BUS MER GYIS KHENGS PA SRAN MA TZAM RE RES KYANG BDE STONG DBYER MED KYI YE SHES SKYE NUS PAR BSAM LA LAN BDUN SOGS BYA'O,,
rows.wylie: smad kyi khams dvangs ma rnams kyang ro rkyang gnyis su zhugs nas ro rkyang gnyis kyi mar sne dbu ma'i nang du bcug nas khams thams cad dbu mar zhugs pas dbu ma smin mtshams nas bha ga'i ba'i bar khams dvangs ma dngul chu lta bus mer gyis khengs pa sran ma tsam re res kyang bde stong dbyer med kyi ye shes skye nus par bsam la lan bdun sogs bya'o
rows.english: Now the purified essence of the substances in the channels of the lower part of the body too enters these two channels--that of taste, and the solitary one.  You have inserted the lower tips of these two channels into the central channel; watch now as all the substances flow into the central channel, filling it from the point between the eyebrows on down to the bhaga with a pure liquid substance shining like quicksilver.  Every single pea-sized drop of this moonsilver would be enough to bring on the wisdom of indivisible bliss and voidness.  Repeat this again for a total of seven times, or however many you've been doing.

rows.wylie: des na 'od gsal rlung stobs kyis zin pa min pas, gnyid ting nge 'dzin du skyed nus pa la ni gnyid kyi 'od gsal gyi sngon du 'char dgos pa'i stong pa gsum sngar bshad pa de mi 'char bas, de gsum sngon du mi 'char ba'i gnyid kyi ting nge 'dzin gsal dvangs byung yang, gnyid kyi 'od gsal gyi don med do
rows.english: What this all means is that, because he or she has not attained recognition of the clear light by force of their work with their winds, then this individual who is able to maintain meditative concentration in their sleep has not managed to get the three types of emptiness to appear, as we described earlier, first--and the fact is that they must appear prior to the clear light of sleep.  And although it may be true that you can achieve a meditative concentration within your sleep which is extremely lucid even without these three having made their appearance, this is not what the "clear light of sleep" refers to.

rows.acip: DE'I PHYIR GNYID KYI 'OD GSAL LA NYAMS DANG RTOGS PA'I 'OD GSAL GNYIS DANG, SRAB MO DANG 'THUG PO'I 'OD GSAL GNYIS DANG, RMI LAM GYI DUS SU RTOG MED KYI TING NGE 'DZIN GSAL DVANGS BYUNG BA YANG, GNYID KYI 'OD GSAL DU 'JOG PA'I RNAM GZHAG MANG PO SNANG YANG SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR MA PHYED PAR GNYID TING NGE 'DZIN DU SKYED NUS PA TZAM GYI STENG NAS BSHAD PA MANG DU BYAS PAR SNANG BAS, YID BRTAN THUB PA MI SNANG NGO,,
rows.wylie: de'i phyir gnyid kyi 'od gsal la nyams dang rtogs pa'i 'od gsal gnyis dang, srab mo dang 'thug po'i 'od gsal gnyis dang, rmi lam gyi dus su rtog med kyi ting nge 'dzin gsal dvangs byung ba yang, gnyid kyi 'od gsal du 'jog pa'i rnam gzhag mang po snang yang sngar bshad pa ltar ma phyed par gnyid ting nge 'dzin du skyed nus pa tsam gyi steng nas bshad pa mang du byas par snang bas, yid brtan thub pa mi snang ngo
rows.english: And so it is that the clear light of sleep can be discussed in terms of the two of a feeling of clear light and an actual experience of clear light; and in terms of the two of a less deep state of clear light and a deeper state of it; and in terms of a clear and lucid state of non-conceptual concentration that comes in your dreams.  And despite the fact that many presentations on the clear light of sleep have been written, a great number of them give their explanation based on nothing more than teaching the ability to turn sleep into a state of meditative concentration, without making any of the distinctions we've just mentioned.  As such it does not appear that we should accept these words as authoritative.

rows.acip: 'DI SKABS SKYON SBYANGS PA LAS BDUD RTZIR BSGYUR MA ZIN LA, DE'I STENG GI BAR SNANG NAS HE RU KA'I NGO BO H'Um DKAR PO YONGS SU GYUR PA LAS KUN DA LTA BU'I BYANG SEMS KYI RANG BZHIN GYI KHA tV'Am GA DKAR PO MAR GYIS BCOS PA LTA BU ZHU LA KHAD 'DRA BA MGO MJUG LDOG STE BDUD RTZI'I DBUS SU LHUNG BA GA YON SKOR LAN GSUM GYI MTHAR LTEM GYIS ZHU BAS RDZAS RNAMS NA BA MED PA SMAN, 'CHI BA MED PA TSE, ZAG PA MED PA YE SHES KYI BDUD RTZIR GYUR NAS BCUD DE DAG MDOG DKAR BA, RO MNGAR BA, REG BYA BSIL BA, NUS PA SHI NAS ZHAG BDUN LON PA'I RO'I KHAR SONG YANG GSO NUS PA LTA BUR GYUR PA NI YON TAN RTOGS PA,
rows.wylie: 'di skabs skyon sbyangs pa las bdud rtsir bsgyur ma zin la, de'i steng gi bar snang nas he ru ka'i ngo bo hUM dkar po yongs su gyur pa las kun da lta bu'i byang sems kyi rang bzhin gyi kha TvAM ga dkar po mar gyis bcos pa lta bu zhu la khad 'dra ba mgo mjug ldog ste bdud rtsi'i dbus su lhung ba ga yon skor lan gsum gyi mthar ltem gyis zhu bas rdzas rnams na ba med pa sman, 'chi ba med pa tshe, zag pa med pa ye shes kyi bdud rtsir gyur nas bcud de dag mdog dkar ba, ro mngar ba, reg bya bsil ba, nus pa shi nas zhag bdun lon pa'i ro'i khar song yang gso nus pa lta bur gyur pa ni yon tan rtogs pa
rows.english: At this point the liquid is only purified of the imperfections; it has not yet become nectar.  Now in the space above there comes a white letter hung, which in its essence is Heruka.  It transforms, and from it comes a khatvanga staff that has the nature of the element of enlightenment which is like kunda.  The staff is white, as though it were made of butter, and seems almost about to melt. The staff turns on its head and falls into the middle of the nectar; it goes around three times to the left and then melts completely.  Now the things in the cup become the nectar of medicine, the end of all sickness; the nectar of life, the end of all death; and the nectar of wisdom, the end of all impurity. These essential fluids now take on a white color.  Their taste is sweet, and they are cool to the touch.  Their potency is as if they could be poured into the mouth of a man who was seven days dead and revive them.  This then is the step we call "realizing the fine qualities."

rows.acip: A'A:S BDUD RTZIR BSGYUR, AOm GYIS MANG POR SPEL BAR BSAM LA 'BRU GSUM LAN GSUM BRJOD NAS NA BA MED PA SMAN, 'CHI BA MED PA TSE, ZAG PA MED PA YE SHES KYI BDUD RTZIR GYUR PAS, BDUD RTZI KHA DOG DKAR PO RO MNGAR BA REG BYA SHIN TU BSIL BA, MYONG BA REG PA MTHONG BA TZAM GYIS SHI NAS ZHAG BDUN SONG RUNG GSOS NGES PA'I NUS PA PHUN SUM TSOGS PAR GYUR PAR BSAM,
rows.wylie: a'a:s bdud rtsir bsgyur, aoM gyis mang por spel bar bsam la 'bru gsum lan gsum brjod nas na ba med pa sman, 'chi ba med pa tshe, zag pa med pa ye shes kyi bdud rtsir gyur pas, bdud rtsi kha dog dkar po ro mngar ba reg bya shin tu bsil ba, myong ba reg pa mthong ba tsam gyis shi nas zhag bdun song rung gsos nges pa'i nus pa phun sum tshogs par gyur par bsam
rows.english: The ah transforms the substance into nectar, and the om causes it to expand.  Imagine this, repeat the three syllables, and think that the substance has become the medicine of eternal health, the life of deathlessness, and the wisdom of the immaculate.  The color of the nectar is silver; its taste is sweet; and it is very cool to the touch.  Think that the liquid has become so miraculous that just through experiencing it--by either touching it with your finger or laying your eyes upon it--it most surely has the power to bring a person who has been dead for seven days back to life.

rows.english: There is, moreover, an example we can use for how, when the three different types of beings with their three karmas look all together at a glass full of something wet and flowing, there start to be three different objects, each confirmed by a valid perception. Suppose there is a ball of red-hot steel; one piece of this ball provides the material cause, and the "mantra of steel" provides a contributing factor. rows.english: Generally speaking, each of the three objects mentioned—the pus and the other two—are things of the type that block other objects from entering into the space which they themselves occupy. It is no contradiction though to say that, in this situation where the beings are looking this way, they are not objects such that they block other things from entering into the space they occupy. This is true for the following reason. A central mountain of the world which is square in shape, and a central mountain of the world which is round in shape, and the like, are objects such that they block other things from entering the space they occupy. Nevertheless, it is possible for both these things to occupy the space taken up by a single central mountain of the world. A red-hot ball of steel is something that's hot, but consider what happens when a person touches it after he has used the mantra of steel on his hand. The sensation that he feels is not a sensation of heat; on the contrary, it is a sensation of something not heat. rows.english: There is, moreover, an example we can use for how, when the three different types of beings with their three karmas look all together at a glass full of something wet and flowing, there start to be three different objects, each confirmed by a valid perception. Suppose there is a ball of red-hot steel; one piece of this ball provides the material cause, and the "mantra of steel" provides a contributing factor. rows.english: Someone again may come and claim the following: Let's consider once more this situation where three different types of beings sit down together and look at a glass full of something wet and flowing. Isn't it true that there is no actual pus and blood there? Because isn't it true that the burning steel and so on in the hells is only something that appears to a person who is born there, but that there is nothing there which actually is these objects? Because isn't it true that there is no one at all who went and made all these kinds of things? And isn't this a fact, because doesn't the text of The Bodhisattva's Way of Life say: Who made the burning steel that acts As the floor of the world of hell? Where did all the mass of flames You find there all come from? The Able Ones have spoken that Everything there like this Is nothing at all other than The mind of what's non-virtue.

rows.english: Yet there is no such problem. The point of this quotation is to say that the burning steel and so on are not something that was created by some unchanging creator being or something like that; by someone who thought it over first and then created them. rows.english: There is, moreover, an example we can use for how, when the three different types of beings with their three karmas look all together at a glass full of something wet and flowing, there start to be three different objects, each confirmed by a valid perception. Suppose there is a ball of red-hot steel; one piece of this ball provides the material cause, and the "mantra of steel" provides a contributing factor. Due to these two, a person who has used the mantra of steel on his hand can touch the ball, but he doesn't undergo any sensation of heat; instead, he feels some other sensation. A person who has not used the mantra on his hand touches the ball and does feel a sensation of heat, and no other kind of sensation.

Suppose there is a ball of red-hot steel; one piece of this ball provides the material cause, and the "mantra of steel" provides a contributing factor. Due to these two, a person who has used the mantra of steel on his hand can touch the ball, but he doesn't undergo any sensation of heat; instead, he feels some other sensation. A person who has not used the mantra on his hand touches the ball and does feel a sensation of heat, and no other kind of sensation.
